core_obligations: Decompose the source: the commutative diagram exhibits the groupoid as the disjoint union of the isotropy groups of representatives of its orbits, mapped by the given isomorphism onto the corresponding union in the target (proof lines 1267-1273).

Match the two decompositions: the hypothesis gives a bijection between the orbit sets, so the two disjoint unions are indexed compatibly, and on each summand the morphism is the given isomorphism of isotropy groups (proof lines 1275-1276).
Conclude: a disjoint union of equivalences of groupoids is again an equivalence, so the morphism is an equivalence of groupoids (proof lines 1276-1278).
proof_roadmap: Read the two groupoids as disjoint unions of their isotropy groups, indexed by their orbits (proof lines 1267-1273).
Use the bijection on orbits and the isomorphisms on the summands to get an equivalence summand by summand (proof lines 1275-1278).
difficulty_reason: The lemma gives a criterion for a morphism of groupoids to be an equivalence: it is enough that the morphism induces a bijection between the orbit sets and, for every object, an isomorphism between the isotropy groups (statement lines 1261-1266). The proof is carried by an explicit commutative diagram that writes each groupoid as the disjoint union of the isotropy groups of representatives of its orbits; because the orbits correspond bijectively, the morphism becomes a disjoint union of isomorphisms of the summands, and a disjoint union of equivalences is an equivalence (proof lines 1267-1278). The substance is the decomposition: the diagram is what turns the two hypotheses into a summand-by-summand statement, and the remaining input is the standard closure of equivalences under disjoint unions. The proof is short but complete and contains no forward reference or omission. H2.
